source: Open Food Facts (https://world.openfoodfacts.org). The photographs are fetched at run time and are CC-BY-SA; this file holds only barcodes and the product names and brands read off the packs, which are Open Food Facts product data under the ODbL (see NOTICE)
how_to_read: Every entry is one photograph, addressed by its barcode: the harness fetches
the front image from the Open Food Facts API, so nothing binary lives in this
repository and anybody can rebuild the same corpus.
'expected' lists the spellings a correct reading may use. Null means the field
is NOT legible on that photograph — and those are the interesting ones: a model
that answers anyway is reciting what it knows about the product rather than
reading the picture in front of it, which is exactly the failure a matrix of
well-known brands has to be able to see.
'tolerated' is for text that IS on the packaging but is not the field's
answer — the per-bar nutrition reference on a chocolate wrapper is not the
net weight, and a promotional '+50g' is not a quantity. A model answering
one of those read the picture and filed it in the wrong place; counting it
as invention would blame it for the opposite of what it did.
